questions.text: In a lottery scheduler with 40 tickets, how we will distribute the tickets among 4 processes P1,P2,P3 and P4 such that each process gets 10%, 5%, 60% and 25% respectively?
questions.solution:
Tickets in proportion to share of 40:
- P1: 10% = 4
- P2: 5% = 2
- P3: 60% = 24
- P4: 25% = 10

Answer: P1-4, P2-2, P3-24, P4-10

questions.text: If there are 32 segments, each size 1k bytes, then the logical address should have
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- 32 segments [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 bits for the segment number
- 1 KB per segment [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 bits for the offset

5 + 10 = 15 bits

Answer: 15 bits

questions.text:
Semaphores are used to solve the problem of
I. Race Condition
II. Process Synchronization
III. Mutual Exclusion
IV. None of the above
questions.solution:
Semaphores (wait/signal) are tools to enforce mutual exclusion and to synchronize processes (ordering, producer-consumer, etc.).

Answer: II and III

questions.text: For the processes listed in the following table, which of the following scheduling schemes will give the lowest average turnaround time?
questions.solution:
Average turnaround time:

- FCFS: A 0-3, B 3-9, C 9-13, D 13-15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (3 + 8 + 9 + 9)/4 = 7.25
- Non-preemptive SJF: A, B, D, C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (3 + 8 + 5 + 11)/4 = 6.75
- SRT: A 0-3, B 3-4, C 4-8, D 8-10, B 10-15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (3 + 14 + 4 + 4)/4 = 6.25
- RR (q = 2) is higher than SRT

Answer: Shortest Remaining Time

questions.text:
Consider the following policies for preventing deadlock in a system with mutually exclusive resources.
I. Processes should acquire all their resources at the beginning of execution. If any resource is not available, all resources acquired so far are released
II. The resources are numbered uniquely, and processes are allowed to request for resources only in increasing resource numbers
III. The resources are numbered uniquely, and processes are allowed to request for resources only in decreasing resource numbers
IV. The resources are numbered uniquely. A process is allowed to request only for a resource with resource number larger than its currently held resources
Which of the above policies can be used for preventing deadlock?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I removes hold-and-wait (all or nothing).
- II, III and IV each impose a single global order on requests (increasing or decreasing), which removes circular wait.

All four prevent deadlock.

Answer: Any one of I, II, III, and IV
